stem: The student wants to describe the method Haskó used in her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Wetlands along the Vellin River support dozens of dragonfly species.
• Ecologist Mirela Haskó wanted to know whether beaver dams affect how many dragonfly species live in these wetlands.
• She counted dragonfly larvae in 24 ponds: 12 behind beaver dams and 12 with no dams.
• Ponds behind beaver dams held nearly twice as many dragonfly species as undammed ponds.
• Haskó concluded that beavers create the slow-moving water that many dragonflies need.
choices: Haskó wanted to know whether beaver dams affect how many dragonfly species live in the wetlands along the Vellin River.
To study the question, Haskó counted dragonfly larvae in 24 ponds, 12 of them behind beaver dams and 12 with no dams.
Haskó found that ponds behind beaver dams held nearly twice as many dragonfly species as ponds that had no dams.
Haskó concluded that beavers help dragonflies by creating the slow-moving water that many of the insects need.
explanation: The goal asks for one stage of the study: the method. Only B tells you what Haskó actually did, counting larvae in 24 ponds split between dammed and undammed sites. The other choices give the study's aim, result, or conclusion.

A.why: You picked the study's aim, the question Haskó asked, but the goal asks how she went about answering it. This choice names Haskó's study but describes the wrong stage of it.

C.why: You picked the study's finding, probably because it is the most interesting note. The goal asks for the method, and this sentence gives the result.

D.why: You picked Haskó's conclusion. It's accurate, but it explains what the results mean instead of describing how the study was done.

stem: The student wants to describe where the Lantern fossil was discovered. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Harlow Ridge fossil collection contains more than 300 plant specimens.
• Most of the specimens are ferns and horsetails roughly 300 million years old.
• One specimen, a fossil seed cone nicknamed "Lantern," is the oldest in the collection.
• Lantern was found in 1987 in a coal seam beneath a farm in Brenner County.
• The cone's scales are preserved in enough detail that each one can be counted.
choices: The Harlow Ridge collection, which includes Lantern, holds more than 300 plant specimens, mostly ferns and horsetails.
Lantern, the oldest specimen in the Harlow Ridge fossil collection, is a seed cone from an ancient plant.
Lantern was discovered in 1987 in a coal seam lying beneath a farm in Brenner County.
Lantern's scales are preserved in such fine detail that researchers can count each one.
explanation: The goal ends with "where the Lantern fossil was discovered," and only one note answers that: a coal seam beneath a Brenner County farm. Choice C makes that location the main point of the sentence.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the whole collection. Lantern appears only in a side clause, and the sentence never says where it was found.

B.why: This choice names Lantern but describes what it is and how old it is, not where it was found. Having the right name in a sentence doesn't make it the right detail.

D.why: You picked a feature of the fossil, its well-preserved scales. That's a real detail about Lantern, but it isn't the discovery site.

stem: The student wants to describe how the Kestrel variety copes with dry conditions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Dunmore Plant Breeding Station has released three sorghum varieties since 2010.
• Amberline (2011) was bred for high grain yield in irrigated fields.
• Kestrel (2015) has roots that reach nearly two meters deep, allowing it to draw water during dry spells.
• Copperhead (2019) resists a fungal leaf disease common in humid regions.
choices: Since 2010, the Dunmore Plant Breeding Station has released three sorghum varieties, one of which is Kestrel.
Released four years after Kestrel, the Copperhead variety resists a fungal leaf disease common in humid regions.
Amberline, released four years before Kestrel, was bred to produce high grain yields in irrigated fields.
Kestrel, released in 2015, has roots nearly two meters deep that let it draw water during dry spells.
explanation: The goal names one variety (Kestrel) and one feature (how it handles dry conditions). Choice D makes Kestrel the subject and tells you its deep roots let it reach water during dry spells.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the whole set of varieties. It mentions Kestrel but says nothing about how Kestrel handles drought.

B.why: This choice mentions Kestrel, but its subject is Copperhead and its disease resistance. Here the right name only serves as a date reference for a different variety.

C.why: This choice uses Kestrel only as a reference point and describes Amberline, a variety bred for irrigated fields, not for dry ones.

stem: The student wants to describe the earthquake activity the network recorded before the 2019 Ardley earthquake. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Saltmarsh Seismic Network was installed along the Corrin Fault in 2009.
• From 2009 to 2018, its sensors recorded an average of 40 small earthquakes per year.
• In 2019, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake struck near the town of Ardley.
• In the year after the Ardley earthquake, the network recorded more than 600 aftershocks.
• Since 2021, the network's data have been shared publicly online.
choices: From 2009 to 2018, the Saltmarsh Seismic Network recorded an average of 40 small earthquakes per year.
In the year after the 2019 Ardley earthquake, the Saltmarsh Seismic Network recorded more than 600 aftershocks.
The Saltmarsh Seismic Network was installed along the Corrin Fault in 2009, ten years before the Ardley earthquake.
Since 2021, data from the Saltmarsh Seismic Network, which recorded the Ardley earthquake, have been shared online.
explanation: The goal limits you to a time period (before 2019) and one thing (recorded earthquake activity). Choice A gives the activity the network recorded from 2009 to 2018, which is the full span before the Ardley earthquake.

B.why: This choice describes recorded earthquake activity, but from the wrong period: the year after Ardley. The goal says "before," and you skipped that restriction.

C.why: This choice falls in the right time period, but it tells you when and where the network was installed, not what earthquakes it recorded.

D.why: You picked a sentence about how the network's data are shared now. It doesn't describe any earthquake activity before 2019.

stem: The student wants to describe the materials used to make the Orchard Coverlet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Penhallow Museum holds four coverlets woven in the 1840s by Thomasina Reyle.
• Reyle learned to weave from her aunt in a mill town in northern England.
• Her best-known coverlet, the Orchard Coverlet, is woven from linen and indigo-dyed wool.
• The Orchard Coverlet's border shows a repeating pattern of apple trees.
• Reyle's later coverlets were woven with cotton bought from local mills.
choices: Reyle, the weaver of the Orchard Coverlet, learned her craft from an aunt in a northern English mill town.
The border of the Orchard Coverlet, Reyle's best-known work, displays a repeating pattern of apple trees.
The Orchard Coverlet, Reyle's best-known work, is woven from linen and from wool dyed with indigo.
Reyle's later coverlets, made after the Orchard Coverlet, were woven with cotton bought from local mills.
explanation: The goal names one textile, the Orchard Coverlet, and one aspect of it: its materials. Choice C makes the coverlet the subject and names its materials, linen and indigo-dyed wool.

A.why: You picked the weaver's biography. The coverlet is named, but the sentence is about how Reyle learned to weave, not what the coverlet is made of.

B.why: This choice is about the right coverlet but describes its design, not its materials.

D.why: This choice does name a material, but it belongs to Reyle's later coverlets, not the Orchard Coverlet. You matched the topic of materials but not the item the goal names.

stem: The student wants to describe the method of Okafor's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Memory T cells are immune cells that help the body respond more quickly to infections it has encountered before.
• In 2022, immunologist Rana Okafor and her team asked how long memory T cells last after a mild influenza infection.
• The team collected blood samples from 140 adult volunteers at regular intervals over three years.
• After three years, memory T cells specific to the virus were still detectable in 118 of the volunteers.
• Okafor concluded that even a mild infection can leave lasting immune protection.
choices: Memory T cells are immune cells that help the body respond more quickly to infections it has met before.
Okafor's team collected blood samples from 140 adult volunteers at regular intervals over three years.
After three years, virus-specific memory T cells were still detectable in 118 of the 140 volunteers.
Okafor concluded that even a mild influenza infection can leave a person with lasting immune protection.
explanation: The goal asks for one stage of the study: the method. Only B says what the team actually did to get its data. It collected blood samples from 140 volunteers at intervals over three years. The other choices give the background, the result, or the conclusion.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the general topic. It explains what memory T cells are, but it says nothing about how Okafor's study was carried out.

C.why: You found the right study but the wrong stage. This sentence gives the finding, meaning what the team discovered, not the method it used to discover it.

D.why: This mentions Okafor by name, so it looks on target, but it gives her conclusion. The goal asked how the study was done, not what she decided it meant.

stem: The student wants to describe how the design of Ferrow Park reflects the site's industrial past. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Halden Riverfront Plan, adopted in 2019, redesigned a two-mile stretch of the city's industrial waterfront.
• Planner Ines Vauclair led the plan's design team.
• The plan's centerpiece is Ferrow Park, built where a freight rail yard once operated.
• The park's walking paths follow the routes of the old rail tracks, and sections of the original rails are set into the pavement.
• The plan also added 600 housing units and a bus line linking the waterfront to downtown.
choices: Ferrow Park, the centerpiece of the Halden Riverfront Plan, was designed by a team led by Ines Vauclair.
Adopted in 2019, the Halden Riverfront Plan redesigned a two-mile stretch of industrial waterfront.
Along with Ferrow Park, the plan added 600 housing units and a bus line connecting to downtown.
Ferrow Park's walking paths trace the old rail tracks, and sections of the original rails line the pavement.
explanation: The goal asks about one feature of one place: how Ferrow Park's design reflects the site's past. D makes the park the subject and gives that detail directly. The paths follow the old freight tracks, and pieces of the original rails are set into the pavement.

A.why: This names Ferrow Park, so it looks right, but it tells you who designed the park. The goal asked how the design connects to the site's history.

B.why: This describes the whole riverfront plan, not the one park the goal names. A sentence about the full project skips the specific feature you were asked to describe.

C.why: This mentions Ferrow Park only in passing. The main clause is about housing and a bus line, which are other parts of the plan.

stem: The student wants to identify the source of Tessaly Spring's water. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tessaly Spring is located in the foothills of the Corran Range.
• It is named for Ada Tessaly, a surveyor who mapped the area in 1891.
• The spring discharges about 40 liters of water per second.
• Its water emerges at a nearly constant 14°C throughout the year.
• Hydrologists have traced the spring's water to rain that falls on a limestone plateau 12 kilometers to the north.
choices: Tessaly Spring's water comes from rain falling on a limestone plateau 12 kilometers to the north.
Tessaly Spring is named for Ada Tessaly, a surveyor who mapped the surrounding area in 1891.
Tessaly Spring, in the foothills of the Corran Range, discharges about 40 liters of water per second.
Tessaly Spring's water emerges from the ground at a nearly constant 14°C throughout the year.
explanation: The goal ends with the exact detail it wants: the source of the water. Only one note answers that, the one about rain on a limestone plateau 12 kilometers north. A is built around that note.

B.why: You chose a sentence about the right spring, but it explains where the name comes from. The goal asked where the water comes from.

C.why: This tells you where the spring is and how much water flows out of it. It says nothing about where that water starts.

D.why: This describes the water's temperature when it comes out of the ground. That is a feature of the water, not its source.

stem: The student wants to describe the orbit of planet c. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The star Orvane-3 has three known planets.
• All three were discovered by the transit method, which detects the slight dimming of a star as a planet passes in front of it.
• Planet b is a rocky world slightly larger than Earth and completes an orbit every 4 days.
• Planet c is a gas giant that takes 211 days to orbit the star.
• Planet d, the outermost of the three, was detected in 2024.
choices: All three planets that orbit Orvane-3 were discovered by detecting the slight dimming of the star.
Planet b, a rocky world slightly larger than Earth, completes one orbit of Orvane-3 every 4 days.
Planet c, a gas giant, takes 211 days to complete one orbit around its star, Orvane-3.
Planet c, a gas giant, is the outermost of the three known planets that orbit Orvane-3.
explanation: The goal names one planet and one feature: planet c's orbit. C makes planet c the subject and gives its orbit directly. It takes 211 days to go around Orvane-3.

A.why: This covers the whole planetary system and how it was discovered. The goal asked about one member of the system and one feature of that member.

B.why: This gives the right kind of detail, an orbital period, for the wrong planet. Check which planet the goal names before you match on topic.

D.why: The notes say planet d is the outermost planet, not planet c. This choice gives planet c a position the notes assign to another planet.

stem: The student wants to describe an accomplishment of Merino's from before she became director of the national public health institute. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lucía Merino is an epidemiologist who has worked in public health for over three decades.
• In 2004, she founded a national registry for tracking outbreaks of foodborne illness.
• In 2011, she was appointed director of the national public health institute.
• As director, she expanded free tuberculosis screening to every regional clinic.
• In 2019, she received an international award for her leadership of the institute.
choices: In 2004, Merino founded a national registry for tracking outbreaks of foodborne illness.
As director, Merino expanded free tuberculosis screening to every regional clinic.
In 2011, Merino was appointed director of the national public health institute.
In 2019, Merino received an international award for leading the health institute.
explanation: The goal has a time limit: before Merino became director in 2011. The only accomplishment in the choices from before that year is the foodborne-illness registry she founded in 2004, so A meets the goal.

B.why: This is a real accomplishment, but it happened while she was director, which is after the point the goal names. You skipped the word "before" in the goal.

C.why: This sentence describes the appointment itself. That is the event the goal uses as a cutoff, not an accomplishment from before it.

D.why: This award came in 2019, eight years after she became director. It also honors her leadership of the institute, so it falls in the wrong period.
